line-cli/flow/ipfix.reference: common line-oriented flow export commands (flow exporter, flow monitor); RFC 3954 (NetFlow v9) and RFC 7011 (IPFIX)
line-cli/flow/ipfix.does: Exports the device's flow records to Woodshed as IPFIX over UDP.
line-cli/flow/ipfix.text:
! Enter in global configuration mode, then save the configuration
flow exporter WOODSHED
 destination 10.1.0.50
 transport udp 4739
 export-protocol ipfix
 template data timeout 60
flow monitor WOODSHED-MONITOR
 exporter WOODSHED
 record <FLOW-RECORD>
interface <MONITORED-INTERFACE>
 ip flow monitor WOODSHED-MONITOR input

parts.title: Enter in global configuration mode, then save the configuration
parts.text:
flow exporter WOODSHED
 destination 10.1.0.50
 transport udp 4739
 export-protocol ipfix
 template data timeout 60
flow monitor WOODSHED-MONITOR
 exporter WOODSHED
 record <FLOW-RECORD>
interface <MONITORED-INTERFACE>
 ip flow monitor WOODSHED-MONITOR input

notes: This Woodshed doesn't receive flows yet, so nothing will arrive. The port is the flow listener's default.
Reference only: not tested on a device; check your device's documentation.

Flow export commands differ more than any other here: some devices use one `ip flow-export destination 10.1.0.50 4739` line with a version keyword, some an exporter and monitor pair as above, some a policy that matches traffic first. Treat this as the list of values to set.
<FLOW-RECORD> is a flow record the device defines (many have a built-in one with addresses, ports, protocol and counters); <MONITORED-INTERFACE> is the interface whose traffic to export.
The template timeout (60 s) makes the device resend its templates every minute, so Woodshed can decode its flows soon after a restart.
line-cli/flow/ipfix.check: Woodshed's Flows view lists the device as an exporter within a minute or two, with its templates and sampling rate.

line-cli/syslog/tcp.reference: common line-oriented logging commands (logging host, logging trap, logging facility, logging source-interface); RFC 5424 severities
line-cli/syslog/tcp.does: Sends the device's log messages, informational and more severe, to Woodshed over TCP.
line-cli/syslog/tcp.text:
! Enter in global configuration mode, then save the configuration
logging host 10.1.0.50 transport tcp port 514
logging trap informational

parts.title: Enter in global configuration mode, then save the configuration
parts.text:
logging host 10.1.0.50 transport tcp port 514
logging trap informational

notes: Reference only: not tested on a device; check your device's documentation.

Before you turn on TCP or TLS logging on a firewall: some firewalls block traffic through them when a TCP or TLS syslog server can't be reached, or its certificate fails, unless a "permit traffic when the log host is down" option is set. Check that option first, or use UDP.

The host command differs most between devices: some take `logging host 10.1.0.50` for UDP 514 alone, some write the transport as `tcp/514` after the address or name the sending interface before it, and some use a `logging server` command instead.
`logging trap` sets the lowest severity sent to log hosts on many devices; others set it on the host line, or accept the number (6) instead of the keyword.
Turn on timestamps in the messages if the device offers it (with milliseconds and the time zone, where it can); Woodshed also keeps the time each message arrived.
line-cli/syslog/tcp.check: The device appears on Woodshed's Dashboard with its first message; if it doesn't, check the device's log host status and Woodshed's Listeners on the Setup page.

notes: Then add this machine in Woodshed: Devices → Add polling, its address, port 161, SNMPv2c and the same community; Test poll shows what answers.

rsyslog/syslog/tcp.reference: rsyslog documentation: the omfwd action (target, port, protocol, TCP_Framing, StreamDriver*), RFC 5424 and RFC 5425
rsyslog/syslog/tcp.does: Forwards this machine's syslog, informational and more severe, to Woodshed over TCP.
rsyslog/syslog/tcp.text:
# /etc/rsyslog.d/60-woodshed.conf: Save as this file, then restart rsyslog (sudo systemctl restart rsyslog)
# Woodshed: forward syslog over TCP (RFC 5424 format).
*.info action(type="omfwd" target="10.1.0.50" port="514" protocol="tcp" TCP_Framing="octet-counted"
       template="RSYSLOG_SyslogProtocol23Format"
       queue.type="LinkedList" queue.size="10000" action.resumeRetryCount="-1")

# Check the file and send a test message
sudo rsyslogd -N1
logger -p user.info "Test message for Woodshed from $(hostname)"

parts.title: Save as this file, then restart rsyslog (sudo systemctl restart rsyslog)
parts.text:
# Woodshed: forward syslog over TCP (RFC 5424 format).
*.info action(type="omfwd" target="10.1.0.50" port="514" protocol="tcp" TCP_Framing="octet-counted"
       template="RSYSLOG_SyslogProtocol23Format"
       queue.type="LinkedList" queue.size="10000" action.resumeRetryCount="-1")

parts.title: Check the file and send a test message
parts.text:
sudo rsyslogd -N1
logger -p user.info "Test message for Woodshed from $(hostname)"

notes: The in-memory queue keeps rsyslog from slowing the rest of the system while Woodshed can't be reached, and retries until it can; up to 10,000 messages wait in it.
rsyslog/syslog/tcp.check: On Woodshed's Dashboard this machine appears as a device within a few seconds of the test message; `woodshed status` counts the messages too.

notes: <CA-FILE> is Woodshed's CA certificate as a PEM file on this machine: download it from Settings → TLS → CA certificate (PEM), for example to /etc/rsyslog.d/woodshed-ca.pem, and check its SHA-256 fingerprint is 3F:9A:1C:07:5B:E2:44:D0:8C:61:2F:A9:73:0E:B5:16:C8:4D:92:E7:01:6B:3A:F5:58:C3:9E:20:7D:B4:4A:11.

notes: Reference only: not tested on a device; check your device's documentation.

Before you turn on TCP or TLS logging on a firewall: some firewalls block traffic through them when a TCP or TLS syslog server can't be reached, or its certificate fails, unless a "permit traffic when the log host is down" option is set. Check that option first, or use UDP.

softflowd/flow/ipfix.text:
# Run softflowd (as root), or put the same options in your distribution's softflowd service settings

parts.title: See what it's exporting
parts.text: softflowctl statistics

notes: This Woodshed doesn't receive flows yet, so nothing will arrive. The port is the flow listener's default.
Reference only: not tested on a device; check your device's documentation.
<INTERFACE> is the network interface to watch, as `ip link` names it.
-t maxlife=60 exports long-running flows every minute, so they show up during an incident rather than when they end.
softflowd sees only the traffic that passes the interface it watches.

Field names differ between devices. Many pages also ask which events send a trap.
web-ui/trap/v2c.check: Search Events for type Traps after saving; pages with a "send test trap" button send one at once.

web-ui/trap/v3.does: The values to enter in the device's SNMP trap (notification) page so it sends traps to Woodshed (SNMPv3).
web-ui/trap/v3.text:
In the device's web page, open its SNMP trap or notification settings and add a receiver
Trap receiver (manager) address: 10.1.0.50
Port: 162
SNMP version: v3
User name: <V3-USER>
Security level: authentication and privacy (authPriv)
Authentication: SHA-256, passphrase <AUTH-PASSPHRASE>
Privacy: AES-128, passphrase <PRIV-PASSPHRASE>
Notification type: trap (not inform), unless the page offers informs and you want them answered
